newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Wreck may have caused Venezuela oilspill-Minister.
newsitem.headline: Wreck may have caused Venezuela oilspill-Minister.

text.p: A sunken wreck in Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo shipping channel may have caused a 25,000 barrel oilspill on February 28, the Venezuelan Transport Minister said Wednesday.
The shipping lane used for more than half of Venezuela's oil exports has seen three serious tanker groundings so far this year, but a officials have yet to explain the cause.

"In the case of the first ship, there is the possibility that it hit something, that it was pierced by a ship, the Explorador, which sank there over 10 years ago," said Venezuela's Transport Minister General Moises Orozco Graterol.
He added that it was possible that the impact with the wreck caused the Nissos Amorgos tanker to leave the buoyed channel.

The sunken ship theory, along with poor maintenance, has long been blamed by shipping agents in the area for the series of groundings. Some say insufficient dredging causes ships to touch bottom, thus losing speed to the extent that they are blown out of the channel by strong winds and currents at this time of year.

The Minister said he was studying the idea of enlarging the channel to meet the growing size of ships using it. This idea has been opposed by environmental groups which say it will exacerbate the salinisation of Lake Maracaibo and contribute to the destruction of wildlife there.

The Minister said U.S. army engineers who originally designed the channel would be called in to study the costs of enlarging the channel or building a deep water port in the Gulf of Venezuela, bypassing the channel altogether.
